title: Tenant activity tiling and point-in-time curation for Console analytics
creator: Melissa Ortega
description:
Background: Console usage analytics need compact, queryable tables for cross-tenant SLA and cost attribution. Current sessionization + wide-denorm approaches produce large, expensive scans and incorrect results for historical queries because we don't consistently capture point-in-time dimensions (model variant, route config, tenant quota tier). Goal: build tiled, point-in-time curated marts that enable: fast per-tenant rollups, accurate time-travel joins for retrospection, and low storage cost via sparse tiling and TTLs.

Scope: design and deliver a set of materialized tables and refresh strategies for tenant activity (invocations, routes, model variants) that: 1) support point-in-time joins at daily granularity, 2) are compact for low-scan analytics queries, 3) have predictable incremental refresh cost and backfill story. This ticket covers schema design, partitioning/cluster strategy, incremental mview implementation, and an initial backfill job.

Out of scope: UI/dashboard changes, advanced ML-powered attribution heuristics (follow-ups).
tasks: Draft schema and tile definition (daily tiles, tenant_id, route_id, active_model_version, invocation_count, token_count, median_latency_ms, cost_estimate_usd)
Prototype storage layout: partition by day, cluster by tenant_id, route_id; evaluate z-order vs compound clustering for Parquet/Delta files
Implement incremental materialized view (mview) using change capture from invocation events and snapshot joins for dimension attributes
Add point-in-time dimension table generator (captures model_variant, route_config, quota_tier as of date)
Write backfill job with windowed processing + idempotent writes and test on sample tenant set
Create unit + integration tests for correctness of time-travel joins and aggregation totals
Add cost/scan budget controls: size-based compaction job and TTL policy for tiles older than 365 days
Document API for Console queries and provide example SQL snippets for common use cases (tenant SLA, cost by model variant, tail-latency analysis)
acceptance_criteria:
- Daily tiled mart exists in the analytics cluster with partitions for each day in the test window.
- Point-in-time joins reproduce historical route/model attribution for a set of 3 sample tenants (gold, standard, trial) with parity to raw-event replay within 0.5% for counts.
- Incremental mview completes within target window (nightly run completes < 2 hours for 30M daily invocations).
- Backfill job can replay 90 days of data for a tenant cohort with progress checkpointing and idempotent commits.
- Query examples demonstrate 5x lower scanned bytes vs current wide invocation table for common analyses.
- Documentation (schema, refresh, runbook) published to Confluence and linked on the ticket.
notes:
Design decisions and trade-offs: we evaluated full denormalized wide tables vs tiled point-in-time marts. Full denorm is simpler for queries but leads to very large daily scans and expensive compactions. Chosen approach: daily tiles + explicit point-in-time dimension snapshots. Trade-offs: slightly more complex join logic and backfill, but significant savings in scan volume and clearer correctness for historical queries.

KV cache consideration: ensure join keys are compact and avoid carrying full payloads into tiles. Cost estimation uses token_count * model_unit_price heuristic; will align with billing engineering to sync prices.

Open questions: optimal tile retention for long-tail tenant audits (legal may request 3+ years), and whether hourly tiling is needed for specific low-latency product SLAs.
